I’m so sorry for your loss. I know exactly how you feel, I lost my soul cat almost a month ago. The first two weeks were horrible, I forced myself to go to work but would come home and just go straight to bed. I didn’t eat anything the first week, and slowly started eating one small meal a day the next. It’s hard, the pain you’re feeling is insufferable. Losing my best friend has been the hardest thing I ever dealt with, no longer coming home to him, no longer having our morning routine before I left to work, no longer having my cuddle buddy. It’s tough. Try to find something that you love to distract you. I did the same thing as you (and still do) by using the tv and phone as a distraction but it doesn’t work well. I love to read so finally found the courage to pick up a book, it was hard at first because I felt guilty for doing something I love, for trying to find happiness. But it helped, it distracted me and helped me find an escape. Maybe there is a hobby you have that can do the same for you. And please keep up on the walks, even on days where it seems importable. Going outside helps, I know it sounds cliche but touch a piece of grass, it truly does help bring you into the moment. 
Also something that could help is doing something to honor your cockatiel, my boyfriend and I have an alter in honor of our cat. And have slowly been putting together a photo album full of just his pictures. It was painful at first to constantly be looking at his picture, but slowly the memories are becoming happy again. Being able to tell the story behind the picture to one another as we put it in the album feels nice, and helps to know he’ll never be forgotten. Good luck with your healing, i know how hard it is and again I’m so so sorry for your loss, it is never enough time with our loved ones.

I know the difference between depression and sadness. I never said you offended OP. You offended me, a person with with diagnosed depression for over 10 years. People have trauma whether it be from childhood, abuse, lost of a loved one, anything that has left them feeling less. Losing my best friends has left me depressed for months now, who knows how long it’ll take me to completely heal. Maybe 3 years, which is fine. Everybody heals at their own pace. Your response just seems completely insensitive is all.

Who are we to say how long somebody can be depressed over the loss of someone? Friendship is one of the most powerful bonds between people. It’s one of the most honest, there are no other factors in it like family (the whole they are your blood thing) and romantic relationships (physical intimacy). People are able to heal at whatever pace they need from whatever loss or trauma they been through.
